Minimax optimization · SETTING 355

Ball-simplex matrix games: arbitrary randomized two-sided matrix-vector queries

CV_S_MG_RANDOM_BALL

Normalized ball-simplex matrix games with arbitrary randomized two-sided matvec queries. Exact zero and one-query endpoints are established by local proofs; the high-dimensional epsilon-dependent randomized lower remains excluded. A full-domain KOS v3 upper is combined with exact reconstruction under the randomized target quantity.

Polynomial gap present

01

Setting specification

Task

Return a feasible strategy pair for the ball–simplex matrix game. Accuracy is measured by the full saddle gap between the two best response values.

$$ \min_{x\in X}\max_{y\in\Delta_m}y^\top Ax,\quad A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}. $$

Admissible model

Assume $A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}$, $B_2^n=\{x\in\mathbb R^n:\|x\|_2\le1\}$, and $\Delta_m=\{y\in\mathbb R^m:y_i\ge0,\ \mathbf1^\top y=1\}$. Also $X=B_2^n$, with each row satisfying $\|A_{i,:}\|_2\le1$.

The dimensions $m,n$ are public and the matrix is hidden. Both strategy domains are compact and convex, ensuring a saddle point.

Oracle interface

Public inputs include matrix dimensions $m,n$ and tolerance $\varepsilon$, together with the declared initial point and feasible-set information. The hidden function, operator, or matrix has no disclosed analytic representation.

$$ (x,y)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}^m\longmapsto(Ax,A^\top y) $$

A pair of left and right matrix products forms one bundled call. Responses are exact, and query vectors need not belong to the strategy domains.

Output

Return $(\widehat{x},\widehat{y})\in X\times\Delta_m$.

The output may be any measurable postprocessing of the history, including an unqueried point, average, or convex combination. It must satisfy the stated domain and feasibility requirements; no additional function value or computable certificate is required.

Loss or accuracy criterion

The global saddle gap subtracts the best value the minimizing player could attain against the returned dual strategy from the best value the maximizing player could attain against the returned primal strategy. The gap must be at most $\varepsilon$ with probability at least $2/3$.

$$ \max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^\top A\widehat{x}-\min_{u\in X}\widehat{y}^\top Au $$

The global gap is finite and nonnegative, and at most $2$ on the normalized class.

The complete gap can be as large as 2 for an arbitrary pair, but the public choice $x=0$ gives gap at most 1 for every matrix. The exact zero-query threshold for this randomized target is therefore $\varepsilon=1$.

Resource accounting

A bundled two-sided call costs $N_{\rm matvec}$. A single right or transpose product can be simulated by setting the other input to zero.

Use a fixed worst-case budget: calls never exceed the prespecified $N$ on any instance or random execution path. Earlier stopping within the budget is permitted.

Count all information calls for one instance and one requested accuracy, including initialization. Exact-real arithmetic, storage, and solving known models from public inputs and returned data are uncharged. This query-complexity quantity does not certify arithmetic or bit complexity.

Algorithm views and success guarantees

Arbitrary measurable sequential adaptive randomized algorithms are allowed. The private seed is independent of the hidden instance. Queries, stopping, and output may use the full history, without additional span, zero-respecting, communication, or memory restrictions.

A single algorithm is chosen from the public input and must satisfy the guarantee for every fixed admissible instance.

$$ \Pr\!\left(\max_{v\in\Delta_m}v^\top A\widehat{x}-\min_{u\in X}\widehat{y}^\top Au\le\varepsilon\right)\ge\frac23. $$

Probability is over private algorithmic randomness only. The unknown instance is fixed before interaction.

Budget convention
fixed_worst_case_cap

proof
/proofs/1/proof · SHA-256 8979e58015e051c5b7064416e78f3f0335a09df942bfc0181d69b6503a8d01ed
If n<=m, query (e_j,0) for j=1,...,n; each bundled response contains the j-th column A e_j. If m<n, query (0,e_i) for i=1,...,m and read each row from A^T e_i. Each is a legal arbitrary-real-vector query and costs exactly one bundled call. The full matrix is then known. A saddle point exists by compact convex strategy sets and bilinearity; exact internal solution is uncharged in this oracle model. The returned feasible pair has gap zero on every instance and every execution, so it meets the target per-instance probability 2/3 for all positive tolerances with pathwise cap min(m,n). This is a direct derivation for q2, not an assertion that the legacy source-scoped q1 is definitionally the same quantity.

proof
/proofs/2/proof · SHA-256 db04f8c875ce852a8a1c9ffdf6e5ec46c8bfd96db688146a366c887c83da5209
For any normalized A and any y in Delta_m, choose x=0. The full saddle gap is max_i (A x)_i-min_{||u||<=1} y^T A u=||A^T y||<=sum_i y_i ||A_i||<=1. Thus zero queries suffice for epsilon>=1, deterministically, in all positive dimensions. For necessity, fix a unit vector a=e_1 in R^n. Let A_+ have every row a^T and A_-=-A_+. Every feasible output (x,y) has gaps 1+a^T x and 1-a^T x respectively. When epsilon<1, their success events are disjoint. A zero-query randomized algorithm has the same output law under both fixed matrices. Consequently the two success probabilities sum to at most one, so at least one is at most 1/2<2/3. This proves N*>=1 for any fixed pathwise cap below one. At epsilon=1 the output x=0 succeeds for both and for the whole class; the boundary is closed on the zero side. If min(m,n)=1, the preceding reconstruction proof uses one call and exactly solves every instance. Hence the endpoint complexity is exactly one below 1 and zero at or above 1. No epsilon^(-2/3) lower bound is inferred.

statement
/proofs/3/statement · SHA-256 b51f375be1ffa6d46e6ce6bd5a231a7f8c3b57d7bf19e3ce2d59c3d535418a4a
For every positive integer m,n and every epsilon>0, the exact target q2 satisfies N*(epsilon)<=min{min(m,n),K_KOS}, where eta=min{epsilon,1/2}, ell_KOS=1+log(2mn/eta), and K_KOS=ceil(C_KOS eta^(-2/3) ell_KOS^(p_KOS)) for universal C_KOS>=1 and p_KOS>=0. No lower-bound dimension window is required.
proof
/proofs/3/proof · SHA-256 830634749b673645bb822c7689cfa490ccc3296b39ae23fa378ef45c114a7a70
Source premise: Karmarkar--O'Carroll--Sidford, arXiv:2601.02347v3, Theorem 1.2, states a deterministic algorithm for every normalized game of this type with tilde-O(eta^(-2/3)) matvecs. Section 1 defines an eta-solution by the complete saddle gap, and its oracle returns the pair (A^T y,Ax). Footnote 3 limits the hidden factors to polylogarithms in m,n,eta^(-1). The source's Section 7.2 proof establishes this theorem without a lower bound on dimension depending on eta. Class/output/metric map: the source class X=B_2^n, Y=Delta_m and max_i ||A_{i,:}||_2<=1 is exactly the present normalized class. Its feasible output pair is a legal target output, and its max_y y^T A xhat - min_x yhat^T A x metric is the target complete gap. Run the theorem at eta=min{epsilon,1/2}. Since eta<=epsilon, its deterministic gap guarantee implies target success probability one, hence at least 2/3, for every fixed admissible matrix. This is a one-way deterministic-witness inclusion into the randomized algorithm class; it transfers no deterministic lower bound. Oracle/cost map: the source pair query is a legal target query because the target allows arbitrary real x,y. One such source pair is answered by exactly one target bundled response (Ax,A^T y), with order exchanged internally if needed. A source implementation that requests one directional product can obtain it using one target call with the other vector zero and discard the extra response. If two directions are requested sequentially, charge the actual two calls; do not divide directional counts by two or merge adaptively dependent queries. Thus the source count is an upper bound on target calls, up to at most a fixed convention factor absorbed in C_KOS. Exact arithmetic, known-domain optimization, and computation from returned data are free in both query models. The source has a deterministic worst-case call bound, so its witness satisfies the target pathwise cap; there is no expectation-to-cap conversion. Uniform integer budget: because m,n>=1 and 0<eta<=1/2, the positive quantity ell_KOS=1+log(2mn/eta) dominates 1, log m, log n and log(1/eta). The source tilde-O bound can therefore be bounded by C_KOS eta^(-2/3) ell_KOS^(p_KOS) for fixed universal C_KOS>=1 and p_KOS>=0, increasing the constant for finite endpoint ranges. Round upward to K_KOS. For m,n>=2 use the source algorithm. When min(m,n)=1, use the separately proved one-call exact reconstruction instead, which is no greater than K_KOS. This handles singleton dimensions without relying on an entropy bound with log(1)=0. The choice eta<=1/2 also handles epsilon>=1 and avoids a false vanishing logarithmic factor. All dimensions are finite and positive, and epsilon=0 is outside the native accuracy domain. Envelope: independently, basis reconstruction costs at most min(m,n) and returns gap zero. Both witnesses are chosen using public dimensions and accuracy, so select the smaller of their public proved integer caps. This proves the displayed min bound directly for q2. The old q1 source-scoped resource record is not identified with q2, and the old narrow b2 record is not needed for the new envelope. On every nonzero comparison updated here, 0<epsilon<2; consequently epsilon/4<=eta<=epsilon and the same upper is written min{min(m,n),tilde-O(epsilon^(-2/3))}, with only the stated positive dimension/precision logarithms suppressed. Existing exact zero and exact one-query rows are sharper and remain selected unchanged. This proves only an upper bound; the separate claimed randomized growing lower remains excluded.

Within positive dimensions and positive tolerance, first split epsilon>=1 from epsilon<1. Below 1, split min(m,n)=1 from min(m,n)>=2; in the latter split by the original source-window H. /joint_analysis/impact/0/argument · SHA-256 cb96035ecbae7df227084eeca52927bd1b8bcf3cc51c362f601c0f8f170fa6d4
Prove the exact ball-simplex zero-query threshold epsilon>=1, improving the earlier sufficient condition epsilon>=2. Add a lower bound N>=1 valid for arbitrary randomized algorithms and close the exact zero/one-query complexity when min(m,n)=1. Independently prove the min(m,n) reconstruction upper bound for q2, without equating it implicitly with the original source-scoped q1. The main high-dimensional window has only a proved constant lower bound and therefore a polynomial gap; the unverified epsilon^(-2/3) lower-bound claim remains excluded.
